Serialize a Submission Profile to Portable JSON

Source: R/serialize_profile.R
write_profile.Rd

Writes a submission_profile – whether a built-in authority profile from submission_profile() or a caller-built one from custom_profile() – to a portable JSON document that can be stored, version-controlled, or shared and later read back with read_profile() into an equivalent, validated profile.

Usage

write_profile(profile, file = NULL, pretty = TRUE)

Arguments

profile

A submission_profile object.

file

Optional path to write the JSON to. When NULL (default) the JSON string is returned; when a path is given the JSON is written there and the path is returned invisibly.

pretty

Logical; whether to pretty-print the JSON with indentation. Defaults to TRUE. The choice does not affect the round-trip as long as it is the same on repeated writes.

Value

When file is NULL, a single JSON string. When file is a path, the path, invisibly.

Details

The serialization carries only values that already exist on the profile; it invents, defaults, or alters no weight, threshold, or other configured value. The document is wrapped in a small envelope recording a schema version so that read_profile() can recognize and check it.

The export is a faithful, stable round-trip: reading a written profile and writing it again produces byte-identical JSON (export, import, export is stable).

See also

read_profile() to read the result back, diff_profiles() to compare a profile against a built-in authority.

Examples

prof <- submission_profile("FDA", "NDA")
json <- write_profile(prof)
cat(json)
#> {
#>   "r4subprofile_schema": 1,
#>   "profile": {
#>     "authority": "FDA",
#>     "full_name": "U.S. Food and Drug Administration",
#>     "country": "United States",
#>     "submission_type": "NDA",
#>     "study_phase": null,
#>     "pillar_weights": {
#>       "quality": 0.35,
#>       "trace": 0.25,
#>       "risk": 0.25,
#>       "usability": 0.15
#>     },
#>     "bands": {
#>       "ready": [85, 100],
#>       "minor_gaps": [70, 84],
#>       "conditional": [50, 69],
#>       "high_risk": [0, 49]
#>     },
#>     "required_indicators": ["Q-MISS-VAR", "Q-TYPE-MISMATCH", "Q-LABEL-LEN", "Q-DUP-RECORDS", "Q-FORMAT-ERR", "T-ORPHAN-VAR", "T-TRACE-LEVEL", "T-AMBIGUOUS-MAP", "T-DERIVATION-DOC", "R-HIGH-RPN", "R-OPEN-RISK", "R-MITIGATION-GAP", "U-DEFINE-COMPLETE", "U-REVIEWER-NOTE", "U-LABEL-QUALITY"],
#>     "required_asset_types": ["dataset", "define", "program", "validation", "spec"],
#>     "minimum_coverage": 0.9,
#>     "rpn_bands": {
#>       "critical": [80, 125],
#>       "high": [40, 79],
#>       "medium": [15, 39],
#>       "low": [1, 14]
#>     },
#>     "default_detectability": 3
#>   }
#> }

# Round-trip back into an equivalent profile:
prof2 <- read_profile(json)
identical(write_profile(prof2), json)
#> [1] TRUE
